input.rationale: Records the executed drift-bound probe (experiment 23d38c5cec9a43a89539bf38b3623b09-experiment, receipt 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4, all nine generated tests passed) and answers the parent investigation's registered gap 838461385f784f74af057837ff488a66-gap-3 from it. The receipt shows the drift is neither bounded nor repaired: eight further re-synchronization rounds took both followers from accepted 6 / decided 6 to accepted 14 / decided 14 one index per round while the leader kept its own accepted index at 6 and its decided index followed to 14 with an unreadable decided log in every round; a leader change onto one of the inflated followers did not reset the accounting (that node kept accepted 14 instead of re-deriving its six indices of content), the previously truthful replica was itself re-synchronized to accepted 7, and in the three following rounds the followers' accepted indexes reached 18 and 10 while the decided index froze at 14 because no write quorum of recorded accepted indexes covered the further reports. No guarded drain, sample or leader change panicked over the eleven rounds. This update therefore (a) revises the parent question-level interpretation into a five-class account, (b) revises knowledge e65d63f4057d4c5bbe8390ac06b30fce-knowledge-2, which claimed the reported decided index follows the drift, into the narrower claim that it follows only while a write quorum covers it and that a leader change re-inflates the truthful replica instead of repairing the accounting, and (c) answers gap-3 as resolved. It also rewrites the parent discriminator to the next open direction and launches the probe for it: the over-compaction case stopsign_overcompaction_then_resync compacts the new leader inside its drifted decided index so that the compacted index moves past the reported accepted index of a live replica, then re-synchronizes that replica (with a replica above the compacted index as a control), so that the decisive observation - a panic or a silently empty suffix on the below-compacted re-synchronization - becomes an executed result rather than a source reading. No other records are changed: the two child accounts (trim, snapshot) and their gaps stand, and the new receipt is cited only for the parent account.

investigations.discriminator: Whether a compaction whose bound comes from the drifted decided index moves the compacted index past a live replica's reported accepted index, so that the next re-synchronization of that replica asks the leader for a prefix below the compacted index. The decisive observation would be a panic or a silently empty suffix on that request rather than a consistent re-sync. The re-synchronization drift itself is no longer the open question: it was shown to continue one index per round over eight rounds, to be unrepairable by a leader change, and not to panic (receipt 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4).

knowledge.statement: Repeated re-synchronizations of replicas that already hold the StopSign make the cluster's reported accepted index drift one further index per round while the log content stays fixed, and while the drifting reporters hold a write quorum the leader keeps adopting the maximum reported accepted index as its decided index: over eight further rounds both followers went from accepted 6 / decided 6 to accepted 14 / decided 14 while the leader's own accepted index stayed 6, its decided index followed to 14 and its decided-log read returned nothing in every round. The drift neither saturates nor is repaired inside the sealed configuration: a leader change onto one of the inflated followers left that node at accepted 14 instead of re-deriving its six indices of content, the previously truthful replica was itself re-synchronized to accepted 7, and in the three following rounds the followers' accepted indexes rose to 18 and 10 while the decided index froze at 14 because no write quorum of recorded accepted indexes covered the further reports.
knowledge.conditions: Three-node cluster after a decided StopSign, each round being a pair of public reconnected() calls addressing the current leader, with nothing else proposed. Observed over three rounds in receipt 6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d (followers 7 then 8 then 9 at events 41, 42, 44, 45, 47, 48; leader decided 7 then 8 then 9 with accepted 6 at events 43, 46, 49) and over eight rounds plus a leader change plus three further rounds in receipt 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4 (baseline accepted 6 / decided 6 events 9-11; followers accepted 7 at events 12, 13 and 14 at events 33, 34; leader accepted 6 with decided 7 and 14 and an unreadable decided log at events 14, 20, 35; after the leader change node 1 at accepted 14 / decided 14, node 2 at accepted 15, node 3 at accepted 7, events 36-38; last round node 2 at accepted 18 and node 3 at accepted 10 with decided 14, events 46, 47; eleven guarded stages with zero panics, event 48). The decided index stopped following once the reports outran every write quorum; no bound on rounds or on the reported values was reached, and the run stopped after eleven rounds by construction.
knowledge.changed_premise: Narrows the claim that the reported decided index always follows the drift. It follows only while the drifting reporters reach a write quorum in the same term: with the new leader's own recorded indexes lagging, the decided index stopped at the drifted value of 14 while the followers' accepted indexes continued to 18 and 10, so the newest drift shows up as accepted indexes that no longer reach a decision. The revision also records that a leader change re-inflates the previously truthful replica instead of repairing the accounting, and that eleven rounds with eleven guarded stages produced no panic.

interpretations.rationale: One index-space error in the StopSign accounting, five witnessed classes of consequence in nine receipts of one lineage, and the drift is neither bounded nor repaired inside the sealed configuration. Cause: sync_log adds the StopSign carried by a LogSync on top of sync_idx plus the suffix length while the sender's resume point may already count that StopSign, and create_log_sync never shifts sync_idx for a StopSign the sender already holds. (1) A replica that already accepted the configuration's StopSign and is given a resume point that covers it ends one index past its content: follower after reconnected() (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35), follower re-promising in an ordinary new term with no reconnected() call (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11), the leader that takes over from such a follower (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13), and two followers under a snapshot-capable entry type (fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 events 51, 52). Each such replica stops reporting its reconfiguration as decided and its decided-log read loses the entries (one element or nothing against six before). (2) The index drifts one step per re-synchronization round rather than settling: three consecutive reconnection rounds took the followers from 7 to 8 to 9 over unchanged content and the leader's decided index followed (6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d events 41-49). (3) A write quorum of drifted reports makes the leader decide the reported index although it holds fewer entries (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 and 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 24; snapshot-capable: fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 event 53), after which the leader no longer reports the reconfiguration as decided and its decided log is unreadable. This decision needs two drifted reporters in a three-node cluster: with one, the leader stayed consistent (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37; 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9). (4) Both compaction paths inherit the drifted values and act on them: trim(None) took the minimum recorded accepted index, which had drifted above the leader's content, and compacted index 7 for a log of six indices, with the region then reported trimmed (ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a events 9-15); snapshot(Some(8), false) was accepted inside the drifted decided index, advanced the compacted index to 8 and produced a snapshot holding none of the five decided entries the log contained, so the entries are no longer reachable and the snapshot that represents them is empty (e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5). Both calls returned success on input the documentation allows. (5) The drift neither saturates nor is repaired, and it does not crash the replicas (2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4). From the healthy baseline of accepted 6 / decided 6 with a readable six-element decided log on all three nodes (events 9-11), eight further rounds of the same two-follower re-synchronization took both followers to accepted 14 / decided 14, one index per round with no saturation (events 12, 13, 18, 19, 33, 34), while the leader's own accepted index stayed 6 and its decided index followed to 14 with its decided-log read returning nothing in every round, from the first round on (events 14, 20, 35). A leader change was then performed onto node 1, one of the inflated followers: it took the lead in a new term and still reported accepted 14 and decided 14 instead of re-deriving its six indices of content (event 36), node 2 reported accepted 15 against decided 14 and node 3 -- the previously truthful leader, which held six indices -- was itself re-synchronized to accepted 7 (events 37, 38), so the drift spread to the replica that had stayed honest rather than being repaired. The three following rounds left the new leader at accepted 14 / decided 14 and took node 2 to accepted 16, 17, 18 and node 3 to accepted 8, 9, 10 while the decided index stayed at 14 (events 39-47): once no write quorum of recorded accepted indexes covers the further reports the decided index stops following, so the later drift appears as accepted indexes that never reach a decision, and the leader's decided index remains thirteen indices above the content it holds and its decided-log read remains unusable (node 2 read an empty decided log at events 45, 46, 47). No guarded drain, sample or leader change panicked over the eleven rounds (event 48: rounds 11, panics 0, 154 messages delivered). Comparisons 0-4 of that receipt are violated with witnesses 33, 34, 35 and 36 (the fifth additionally records nodes 2 and 3 as outside its applicability); comparisons 5-7 came out unknown because their declared admissions put a node condition on the prerequisite and a node-less identity on the panic event, so those states are asserted from the sampled events named above rather than from comparison outcomes. Controls: the pre-change samples and the no-reconnect control kept six indices of content, a six-element decided log, the StopSign at its own index and the reconfiguration reported as decided (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11, 19-21; 6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d events 38-40; fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 events 48-50; 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4 events 9-11).

838461385f784f74af057837ff488a66-gap-3.explanation: Resolved by the drift-bound receipt 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4: nothing inside the sealed configuration bounds or repairs the drift within the tested range. Eight further re-synchronization rounds kept adding exactly one index per round to both followers (accepted 7 at events 12, 13 up to accepted 14 at events 33, 34) while the content stayed at six indices and the leader's decided index followed to 14 with an unreadable decided log in every round (events 14, 20, 35). The leader change is not a repair: the new leader, itself re-synchronized earlier, kept its inflated accepted index of 14 rather than re-deriving six (event 36), and the replica that had remained truthful until then was re-synchronized to accepted 7 (event 38). The drift then continued as accepted indexes only: node 2 reached 16, 17, 18 and node 3 reached 8, 9, 10 while the decided index froze at 14 (events 39-47), so the bound on the decided index in this pattern is quorum arithmetic rather than an explicit limit, and no counter, storage guard or automatic repair was observed at any stage. Eleven guarded stages with 154 delivered messages produced zero panics (event 48), so the unrepaired drift is silent: every call succeeded and no endpoint reported an error.

the decided-log read loses the entries after such a re-synchronization

the leader decides the reported accepted index without bounding it to its own log

counterevidence: The no-reconnect control kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11; 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4 events 9-11), and in the newterm case the new leader and the node that received nothing stayed consistent (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 events 9, 10), so the deviation follows a re-synchronization whose resume point covers the StopSign.

The leader-side decision at a drifted index requires a write quorum of drifted reporters in one term (two of three nodes); one drifted reporter left the leader consistent (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37; 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9), and in the drift-bound receipt the decided index stopped advancing once the reports outran every write quorum (2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4 events 46, 47 against decided 14).

The compaction consequences need the drift to cover every node the bound is derived from: trim's bound is the minimum recorded value, so a truthful replica would keep it honest (76cabb0efc3b4eda8eda8c9c79025550-interpretation-0), and the snapshot witness used a request strictly inside the drifted decided index because the StopSign equal case lowers the bound.

The documented reconfiguration flow expects a new instance once a node observes StopSign(ss, true), narrowing the window in which a user reads the old instance; the drift still hides that observation from the leader and, once compaction acts, removes the entries themselves.

The drift cannot be turned into new client values through the append path: append() refuses with PendingReconfigEntry while a StopSign is stored, which is the case throughout every observed drifted state, so the consequence set stays with index accounting, readability and compaction rather than with mis-assigned entries.
limitations: The drift was exercised for eleven rounds with one mid-run leader change; that range found no bound and no repair, but the decided index stopped following once the reports outran every write quorum, so how far the decided index can keep following is a quorum property that was observed with one three-node pattern rather than characterised in general.
Loss-triggered and timer-triggered re-synchronization were not exercised; the producers observed are explicit reconnected() calls and an ordinary leader change onto a node that had already drifted.

Only three-node clusters were used, with in-memory storage, no persistence across restarts and one snapshot-capable entry type; the compaction witnesses depend on that entry type's snapshot semantics.

Several comparisons in the repeated-rounds, trim, snapshot and drift-bound receipts came out unknown because their admissions shared event names across cases in one execution or put a node condition on the prerequisite; those states are asserted from the sampled operands, with the violated comparisons cited above.

The drift-bound case samples after each drained round, so it does not show intermediate states inside a round, and it does not exercise the forwarded compaction messages that a snapshot or trim call would send to peers.

The consequence set stays within index accounting, readability and compaction; the sealed configuration admits no further entries and refuses appends while the StopSign is stored, so no value is mis-assigned.

scope.description: Ten cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network; the new case drives the drift, changes the leader, compacts the new leader past a live replica's reported accepted index and then lets that replica re-synchronize, reporting any panic as an event field rather than aborting the run.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot; ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } with default ServerConfig (batch_size 1); BLE messages are dropped, as in the lineage.

Three rounds of node1.reconnected(3) plus node2.reconnected(3) reproduce the drifted state (followers accepted 9, leader decided 9 over six indices of content); node1.try_become_leader() then makes node 1 the leader and re-synchronizes the other two, which in the lineage left node 3 at accepted 7 against the drifted decided index.

The snapshot is requested with the leader's own decided index as the bound and local_only = true, so no Compaction message is sent to the peers and the compacted index becomes that decided index (the StopSign is no longer counted as decided in the drifted state, so the bound is not lowered).

reconnected(pid) is called with the current leader, because the library only starts a re-synchronization when the peer named is the leader; every drain and sample runs inside catch_unwind, so a panic inside a handler becomes an event field instead of aborting the run.
excluded: No entry type with use_snapshots() true is used in the new case, so the snapshot branch of create_log_sync is not exercised there.
No load, timer, message loss or node restart is exercised; only reconnected() calls and one leader change.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

parameters.compaction_bound: the new leader's own decided index at the time of the call

experiment.prefix: Same prefix as the lineage: node 3 leads, five entries are appended and decided, then a StopSign is proposed with reconfigure() and decided, so every node holds six indices of content and reports accepted 6 / decided 6 (OVER_BASE). The new case then performs three rounds of node1.reconnected(3)+node2.reconnected(3), each drained and sampled per node as OVER_R{k}_N{pid} for k = 1..3, reads the leader's decided index, elects node 1 with try_become_leader() and samples as OVER_AFTER_CHANGE, calls node1.snapshot(Some(decided), true) and emits OVER_SNAP with the outcome, the panicked flag, the compacted index, the accepted index and the decided index of the leader, then calls node3.reconnected(1) (the replica whose reported accepted index is below the compacted index) with a guarded drain and samples, emits OVER_LAG_RESULT with the panicked flag, repeats the same for node2.reconnected(1) as the control and emits OVER_AHEAD_RESULT, and finally emits OVER_RUN_END with the number of messages delivered. Every sample records accepted_idx, decided_idx, decided_eq_accepted, is_reconfigured, the read of index 5, the read of index 6, the read of the decided suffix from 0 and its length.
semantic_changes: Adds the over-compaction case stopsign_overcompaction_then_resync and the resync_guarded helper; every previously generated case is unchanged apart from sharing one execution.
No production code was modified.

comparisons.description: The snapshot call that compacts the leader inside its drifted decided index completes on its own without panicking.

The re-synchronization of the replica whose reported accepted index lies below the compacted index is handled without a panic: no handler may be brought down by a prefix request below the compacted index.

Control: the replica whose reported accepted index is at or above the compacted index re-synchronizes without a panic, so any panic in the other stage is not attributable to re-synchronization as such.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds the over-compaction case stopsign_overcompaction_then_resync: three re-synchronization rounds, a leader change onto one of the inflated followers, a local snapshot on that leader inside its drifted decided index, and then the re-synchronization of the replica whose reported accepted index is below the resulting compacted index, with a replica whose index is at or above it as a control. Every drain and every sample is panic-guarded. Previously generated cases are unchanged.

investigations.question: When a replica that has already accepted its configuration's StopSign is re-synchronized by the leader (PrepareReq -> Prepare -> Promise -> AcceptSync, e.g. after a re-established connection), does its reported accepted index stay within its actual log content, so that the StopSign keeps being observable as decided (decided index == accepted index) and the decided log keeps being readable?
investigations.hypothesis: No. create_log_sync passes the follower's accepted index (which already counts its stored StopSign as one index) as LogSync.sync_idx; sync_log sets accepted_idx = sync_idx + suffix.len() and then adds 1 again because the LogSync carries the StopSign, so the re-synchronized replica's accepted index becomes one larger than its log content while its decided index stays at the real StopSign position. The replica then reports the inflated index in Accepted, so a write quorum of inflated reports lets the leader set a decided index beyond the entries it can read.
investigations.discriminator: Whether anything inside the sealed configuration bounds or repairs the drift - a counter or storage limit, or a later leader change - after many more re-synchronization rounds; the decisive observation would be the reported accepted and decided indices and the readable decided log after further rounds and further leader changes. The library's own reconfiguration handoff is already narrowed out (the StopSign carries only the next configuration and metadata while the documented flow builds the new instance with fresh storage), and the drifted values' effect on the compaction paths is settled in the trim and snapshot child accounts.

gaps.question: Which legitimate producer path can hand a leader a LogSync whose sync_idx already covers the sender's own StopSign, i.e. whose receiver's accepted index is inflated by the unconditional +1?

investigations.question: Does the drifted accepted index reach the trim decision? The leader derives its trim index from the minimum of the accepted indexes it has recorded for the configuration's nodes, and those recorded values are exactly the ones the re-synchronization inflates; the documented contract instead requires that all nodes have decided the trim index. knowledge.statement: When a candidate becomes leader it adopts two independently ordered inputs in one call: the log comes from the promise that is strictly greatest under (n_accepted, accepted_idx) with pid only as tiebreak, while the decided index is the maximum decided index over all recorded promises; sync_log then writes that decided index and the adopted log in the same storage transaction, and the leader path contains no clamp comparing the two.
knowledge.conditions: Reached in handle_majority_promises after a prepare quorum (leader.rs 257-285) together with set_promise (util.rs 131-149) and get_max_decided_idx (util.rs 168-177); the two orders coincide whenever the promise with the greatest accepted round and index also reports the greatest decided index, which is the case in every observed run of this investigation. Sourced only; no execution has yet produced a disagreement between the two orders.

knowledge.statement: For a candidate that syncs from the greatest promise, the accepted index it ends with is the adopted promise's own accepted count whenever the resume point lies inside that promise's content: sync_idx is the candidate's decided or accepted index, the suffix is the adopted promise's log from there, and the carried StopSign adds the same one index the adopted promise already counted, so the two accounting terms cancel. Whenever the resume point lies beyond that content the suffix is empty and the candidate ends at sync_idx plus the StopSign term. A disagreement between the adopted decided index and the entries held therefore needs some promise reporting a decided index above the adopted promise's content.
knowledge.conditions: Follows from the two branches of the follower's Promise (common_prefix = prep.decided_idx when na > prep.n_accepted, prep.accepted_idx when equal and greater) and sync_log's accepted accounting; the adopted promise is the strictly greatest under (n_accepted, accepted_idx). Sourced; the three-node runs of this investigation had the greatest promise also reporting the greatest decided index, so the disagreement never arose there.

knowledge.statement: Repeated re-synchronizations of replicas that already hold the StopSign make the cluster's reported accepted and decided indices drift one further index per round while the log content stays fixed: the leader keeps adopting the maximum reported accepted index as its decided index, so the reported decided index follows the drift while the leader's own accepted index does not, leaving its decided index above the entries it holds and its decided-log read unusable.

knowledge.statement: Trim's bound is the minimum of the leader's recorded accepted indexes and both trim paths respect it: with no explicit index that minimum is used, and an explicit index above it is refused with that same minimum reported. The bound can therefore exceed only the content of replicas whose recorded accepted index has itself drifted; a replica whose report is still truthful keeps the bound at or below its own content, and no in-cluster promise or log sync can then ask for a prefix below the compacted index.

knowledge.statement: The snapshot path bounds a user-supplied index by the decided index of the node that receives the call, not by any recorded accepted index and not by another node's decided index: an index equal to that decided index is mapped to the decided log without the StopSign, a lower index is used as given, and a greater index is refused with the decided index reported; the snapshot itself is then created from the storage range that starts at the current compacted index.

history.statement: The snapshot path bounds a user-supplied index by the leader's decided index, not by any recorded accepted index and not by another node's decided index: an index equal to the decided index is mapped to the decided log without the StopSign, an index below it is used as given, and a greater index is refused with the decided index reported. knowledge.statement: On a leader whose decided index has drifted above its content, the snapshot path accepts a user-supplied index inside that drifted decided index, advances the compacted index to it, and builds the snapshot from a storage range that starts at the previous compacted index; when that range lies past the entries the log holds, the storage returns nothing and the snapshot is created from an empty slice, so the entries are no longer reachable through the log and the snapshot that now represents the region holds none of them.
knowledge.conditions: Snapshot-capable entry type (Snapshot::use_snapshots() true) with a snapshot that records its input entries; three-node cluster after a decided StopSign, three reconnection rounds giving decided 9 over six indices of content, then snapshot(Some(8), false) on the leader. knowledge.statement: Both compaction paths derive the index they may compact from values the node computes for itself rather than from what any replica holds: trim takes the minimum of the accepted indexes the leader has recorded for the configuration (or refuses an explicit index above that minimum) and the snapshot path takes the decided index of the node that receives the call, while neither bound is compared against the entries the node's own log contains. The consequences follow from that: with the recorded or decided values drifted above the content, trim compacted index 7 and the snapshot path compacted index 8 for logs of six indices.
knowledge.conditions: Capture snapshot; leader role for trim, any role for the snapshot call. knowledge.statement: The snapshot path adjustment for a request equal to the decided index is not a protection against the witnessed drift: that case maps the request to the decided log without the StopSign, which in the observed state was 8 against content of six indices, so the resulting compacted index still exceeded the entries the replica held and the snapshot was still built from an empty range.

scope.description: Two cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network: (resync) re-established connections to the leader after a decided StopSign, (control) identical prefix without reconnected(). Only public API calls drive the protocol; every observation is one CA_EVENT JSON line on stdout.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot, so T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() is false and create_log_sync takes its no-snapshot branch.
ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } (majority 2) and default ServerConfig (batch_size 1, no batching).
Leadership is established with the public try_become_leader() on node 3; BLE heartbeat messages are dropped because no tick() is called.
All SequencePaxos messages are delivered in FIFO order without loss, so the reconnection and re-synchronization is the only deviation from a healthy run.
Case labels in the events ('case') keep the resync and control streams distinguishable.
excluded: Snapshots, trimming and compaction are not exercised; batching is disabled (batch_size 1).
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

basis.prefix: Cluster::new() builds OmniPaxos<Value, MemoryStorage<Value>> for pids 1,2,3 (validated OmniPaxosConfig). run_prefix(): node 3 calls try_become_leader(); the FIFO pump drains Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync/Accepted until quiet (SAMPLE phase leader_elected); node 3 appends Value(0..4) and the pump drains AcceptDecide/Accepted/Decide until quiet (phase entries_decided); node 3 calls reconfigure(ClusterConfig{configuration_id: 2, nodes:[1,2,3]}, None) and the pump drains AcceptStopSign/Accepted/Decide until quiet (phase stopsign_decided). Case resync then calls node1.reconnected(3) and node2.reconnected(3) and pumps to quiet; case control only pumps again. Each SAMPLE line reports node, accepted_idx (get_accepted_idx), decided_idx (get_decided_idx), decided_eq_accepted, is_reconfigured(), read(5), and read_decided_suffix(0) (state plus entry count).
basis.responsibility: Target-internal bookkeeping: SequencePaxos::create_log_sync plus InternalStorage::sync_log decide what a re-synchronized replica's accepted index and carried StopSign are; the caller only reports a re-established connection through the public reconnected() API and never supplies log indices or StopSign state.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading of the re-synchronization path (PrepareReq -> Prepare -> Promise -> AcceptSync -> Accepted) suggests that a replica which has accepted the StopSign gets its accepted index inflated by one when it is re-synchronized at the same ballot: in handle_promise_accept the leader calls send_accsync, whose first branch uses the follower's own accepted index as the valid prefix (leader.rs 150-191), and that index already includes the StopSign because set_stopsign adds it (internal_storage.rs 503-512). create_log_sync then reports that index as LogSync.sync_idx with the sender's StopSign attached, and sync_log adds the StopSign once more, so the follower's accepted index ends at prefix + suffix + 1 while its decided index is the AcceptSync's decided index (internal_storage.rs 313-360). The follower then reports that inflated index in Accepted (follower.rs 112-126), and the leader's decision rule accepts any incoming accepted index whose count reaches a write quorum (leader.rs 316-345), so a write quorum of inflated reports would set the leader's decided index past the entries it holds. Both endpoints this reading endangers are public: is_reconfigured() is gated on stopsign_is_decided() (mod.rs 284-290, state_cache.rs 123-126), the bool of LogEntry::StopSign is documented as 'the reconfiguration has been decided' (util.rs 277-279), and the documented user flow reads the decided suffix and switches configuration only on StopSign(.., true) (reconfiguration.md 25-34). The final judgment is left unresolved until the two-case execution samples the endpoints; the reading also predicts that a fresh or lagging follower, whose prefix does not yet contain the StopSign, is unaffected. Counterevidence and limits: the reconfiguration documentation tells the user to start a new instance once the StopSign is observed as decided, so the affected window is an old instance that keeps running after (or while) it observes the decision and then re-synchronizes; the accounting is correct whenever sync_idx stays at or below the StopSign's own index, which covers the normal catch-up path; the account rests on static reading of the read() combination paths and of MemoryStorage's empty-range behaviour, not on an executed observation.

Confirmed by execution: the re-synchronization of a replica that already accepted its configuration's StopSign inflates its reported accepted index by one, and a write quorum of such reports makes the leader decide an index past every entry it holds. Receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8, two cases in one run over three real OmniPaxos instances with MemoryStorage (events: 19,20,21 = after the StopSign was decided on all three nodes; 22,23 = the two re-synchronized followers; 24 = the leader; 9,10,11 = the identical prefix without reconnected()). Before the re-synchronization all three nodes reported accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, read(5) = StopSign with decided = true, and read_decided_suffix(0) = six elements. After both followers called reconnected(3): node 1 and node 2 reported accepted 7 over the same six indices of content, their read(5) returned None (the StopSign is now placed at index 6 by the internal index-type rule), and their decided-log read from 0 returned a single element (the StopSign), so the five decided entries disappeared from the readable decided log while is_reconfigured stayed true; node 3 (leader) reported decided 7 with accepted 6, is_reconfigured false where it had been true, read(5) = StopSign with decided = false, and read_decided_suffix(0) = None, i.e. the user on the leader can no longer read the decided log at all and never observes the reconfiguration as complete. The declared comparisons match this reading: comparison 2 (leader reports the reconfiguration as decided) violated at index 24, comparison 3 (decided index covered by entries held) violated at index 24, comparison 4 (leader's decided log readable from 0) violated at index 24, comparison 5 (re-synchronized follower's decided log still has the five entries plus the StopSign) violated at indices 22 and 23, while comparisons 0 and 1 (the same predicates before the reconnection, indices 19-21) and comparisons 6 and 7 (the no-reconnect control, indices 9-11) hold, which attributes the change to the re-synchronization rather than to the reconfiguration or to the sampling.

(2) The trigger is not limited to reconnected(): the same resume point arises whenever a leader hands a follower an AcceptSync whose sync_idx already covers the StopSign, which includes the ordinary path where a follower re-promises in a new term and its promise round equals the leader's own promise round (send_accsync's second branch, leader.rs 150-191) or where a candidate leader's decided index becomes sync_idx (create_log_sync in the follower's Promise path, mod.rs 405-432). The submitted successor case tests that ordinary path by cutting off node 2 and letting node 1 take the lead in a new term with only node 3's promise; the source reading predicts node 3 ends inflated (accepted 7 over six indices) with its endpoint and decided log corrupted, while the new leader and the cut-off node stay consistent. The comparison baseline and controls remain the same-run ones: the pre-re-synchronization samples (events 19-21) and the no-reconnect control (events 9-11 and the control case of the successor) held for the same predicates.

e40cd046de9e4f37b5761260b8dc599e-gap-1.explanation: Resolved by the two receipts: the two positions of the decided index were both observed. With two inflated reporters the leader's decision at index 7 pushed the re-synchronized replicas' decided index to 7, so their read of the decided log from 0 returned the StopSign alone (one element) where it had returned six (receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 19, 20 against 22, 23; reproduced in receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 events 22, 23). With one inflated reporter the replicas' decided index stayed at 6 while their accepted index rose to 7, so the same read returned an empty list (receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35 against its own pre-state at event 19 and the untouched nodes at events 36, 37). The generalization is therefore the observed behaviour of both positions, not an extrapolation.

e40cd046de9e4f37b5761260b8dc599e-gap-2.explanation: Partly resolved by source reasoning, partly open. On the snapshot half: in the observed configuration the sender's decided index equals the resume point, so create_log_sync does not take the snapshot branch even with T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() true (mod.rs 405-432), and when that branch is taken it sets sync_idx to the compacted index derived from get_decided_idx_without_stopsign (internal_storage.rs 385-412, 469-474), which excludes the StopSign; the inflation therefore does not depend on the snapshot option, but a snapshot-enabled run has not been executed. No execution has yet sampled a leader inflated in its own accepted index.

interpretations.rationale: Source trace only, no execution. handle_majority_promises pairs two independently ordered inputs: the log_sync of the promise that is strictly greatest under (n_accepted, accepted_idx) (set_promise only replaces max_promise_meta on a strict Greater, and PromiseMetaData's ordering ignores decided_idx) and the maximum decided_idx across all recorded promises (get_max_decided_idx). sync_log then stores the adopted decided index together with the adopted log and does not clamp. Because the decided index adopted is a different node's report, a history in which the greatest-accepted promise holds fewer entries than another promise's reported decided index would leave the new leader reporting a decided index beyond the entries it holds; every observed run so far has the two orders coincide (the greatest-accepted promise was also the greatest decided reporter), so no witness exists. The suspicion is therefore unresolved rather than refuted: the reachability argument I can give (a decided entry must be accepted by a write quorum that intersects every read quorum, so the greatest-accepted promise should cover it) is exactly the protocol invariant that this code relies on instead of a local bound, and I have not turned it into a reachable disagreement history.

interpretations.rationale: Source trace plus a narrowing argument, still without an execution. handle_majority_promises pairs two independently ordered inputs: the log from the promise that is strictly greatest under (n_accepted, accepted_idx) (set_promise replaces max_promise_meta only on a strict Greater; PromiseMetaData's ordering ignores decided_idx) and the decided index from the greatest decided_idx over all recorded promises (get_max_decided_idx); sync_log stores both without clamping, and the leader path has no counterpart to the follower's update_decided_idx_and_get_accepted_idx. For the pairing to break the adopted decided index must exceed the entries the adopted log provides, which requires a promise whose reported decided_idx is greater than the content the leader ends up holding. Narrowing: in the configurations examined here the interposing +1 for a carried StopSign keeps the adopted accepted index at or above the adopted decided index whenever the greatest-accepted promise is the one holding the decided prefix - in the resync/newterm/staleleader runs the followers reported decided 7 with content 6 and the greatest-accepted promise was exactly such a replica, so the leader's post-sync accepted index (sync_idx + suffix + 1) came out at 7 as well and the two matched. A disagreement therefore needs a promise reporting a decided index above its own content while not being the greatest-accepted promise, which none of the observed anomalies produced for the adopted maximum. The suspicion stays unresolved rather than refuted: the protocol argument (a decided entry is accepted by a write quorum intersecting every read quorum, so the greatest-accepted promise should already cover it) is exactly what this code relies on instead of a local bound, and I have neither constructed a reachable disagreement nor bounded it with an execution.

interpretations.rationale: Refuted as an independent defect by source arithmetic, with the residual dependence stated. The candidate's accepted index after the prepare phase is determined by the adopted promise: with the resume point inside that promise's content the candidate ends at exactly the adopted promise's accepted count, because the suffix supplies the entries from the resume point to that content and the carried StopSign adds the same one index the adopted promise had already counted (the follower's Promise sets common_prefix to the candidate's decided index when its accepted round is higher, and to the candidate's accepted index when the rounds are equal and it is further ahead); with the resume point beyond that content the suffix is empty and the candidate ends at the resume point plus the StopSign term. In both cases the candidate's accepted index is at least the adopted promise's content, so for the adopted decided index to exceed the entries held some promise must report a decided index above the adopted promise's content. For truthful reports that is excluded by the protocol's own invariant that a promise with a higher accepted round covers everything decided - the property this code relies on instead of a local clamp - and for corrupted reports the only producers observed in this investigation are the inflated accepted indexes already covered by the parent question, which also leave the adopted decided index equal to or below the leader's accepted index in the newterm and staleleader stages. The two orderings coincided in every observed run, and no run produced a decided index above the adopted log's content, so the suspicion is refuted in its independent form while the residual case (a legal history in which the greatest-accepted promise is not the greatest decided reporter and the invariant fails) remains only as a consequence of the parent's corruption.

investigations.question: When a replica that has already accepted its configuration's StopSign is re-synchronized by the leader (PrepareReq -> Prepare -> Promise -> AcceptSync, e.g. after a re-established connection), does its reported accepted index stay within its actual log content, so that the StopSign keeps being observable as decided (decided index == accepted index) and the decided log keeps being readable?
investigations.hypothesis: No. create_log_sync passes the follower's accepted index (which already counts its stored StopSign as one index) as LogSync.sync_idx; sync_log sets accepted_idx = sync_idx + suffix.len() and then adds 1 again because the LogSync carries the StopSign, so the re-synchronized replica's accepted index becomes one larger than its log content while its decided index stays at the real StopSign position. The replica then reports the inflated index in Accepted, so a write quorum of inflated reports lets the leader set a decided index beyond the entries it can read.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a compaction whose bound comes from the drifted decided index moves the compacted index past a live replica's reported accepted index, so that the next re-synchronization of that replica asks the leader for a prefix below the compacted index. The decisive observation would be a panic or a silently empty suffix on that request rather than a consistent re-sync. The re-synchronization drift itself is no longer the open question: it was shown to continue one index per round over eight rounds, to be unrepairable by a leader change, and not to panic (receipt 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4).

knowledge.statement: When a candidate becomes leader it adopts two independently ordered inputs in one call: the log comes from the promise that is strictly greatest under (n_accepted, accepted_idx) with pid only as tiebreak, while the decided index is the maximum decided index over all recorded promises; sync_log then writes that decided index and the adopted log in the same storage transaction, and the leader path contains no clamp comparing the two.
knowledge.conditions: Reached in handle_majority_promises after a prepare quorum (leader.rs 257-285) together with set_promise (util.rs 131-149) and get_max_decided_idx (util.rs 168-177); the two orders coincide whenever the promise with the greatest accepted round and index also reports the greatest decided index, which is the case in every observed run of this investigation. Sourced only; no execution has yet produced a disagreement between the two orders.

knowledge.statement: For a candidate that syncs from the greatest promise, the accepted index it ends with is the adopted promise's own accepted count whenever the resume point lies inside that promise's content: sync_idx is the candidate's decided or accepted index, the suffix is the adopted promise's log from there, and the carried StopSign adds the same one index the adopted promise already counted, so the two accounting terms cancel. Whenever the resume point lies beyond that content the suffix is empty and the candidate ends at sync_idx plus the StopSign term. A disagreement between the adopted decided index and the entries held therefore needs some promise reporting a decided index above the adopted promise's content.

The drift neither saturates nor is repaired inside the sealed configuration: a leader change onto one of the inflated followers left that node at accepted 14 instead of re-deriving its six indices of content, the previously truthful replica was itself re-synchronized to accepted 7, and in the three following rounds the followers' accepted indexes rose to 18 and 10 while the decided index froze at 14 because no write quorum of recorded accepted indexes covered the further reports.

knowledge.statement: Trim's bound is the minimum of the leader's recorded accepted indexes and both trim paths respect it: with no explicit index that minimum is used, and an explicit index above it is refused with that same minimum reported. The bound can therefore exceed only the content of replicas whose recorded accepted index has itself drifted; a replica whose report is still truthful keeps the bound at or below its own content, and no in-cluster promise or log sync can then ask for a prefix below the compacted index.
knowledge.conditions: Leader role, reached from the public trim() with None or Some(index); follows from the derivation at mod.rs 141-170 and the minimum helper at util.rs 186-191 together with the witnessed drift, in which every recorded value is at or above the compacted index. knowledge.statement: The snapshot path bounds a user-supplied index by the decided index of the node that receives the call, not by any recorded accepted index and not by another node's decided index: an index equal to that decided index is mapped to the decided log without the StopSign, a lower index is used as given, and a greater index is refused with the decided index reported; the snapshot itself is then created from the storage range that starts at the current compacted index.
knowledge.conditions: Leader or follower role; reached from the public snapshot() with Some(index) or None. history.statement: The snapshot path bounds a user-supplied index by the leader's decided index, not by any recorded accepted index and not by another node's decided index: an index equal to the decided index is mapped to the decided log without the StopSign, an index below it is used as given, and a greater index is refused with the decided index reported. The snapshot itself is then created from the storage range that starts at the current compacted index.
history.conditions: Leader or follower role; reached from the public snapshot() with Some(index) or None. knowledge.statement: On a leader whose decided index has drifted above its content, the snapshot path accepts a user-supplied index inside that drifted decided index, advances the compacted index to it, and builds the snapshot from a storage range that starts at the previous compacted index; when that range lies past the entries the log holds, the storage returns nothing and the snapshot is created from an empty slice, so the entries are no longer reachable through the log and the snapshot that now represents the region holds none of them.
knowledge.conditions: Snapshot-capable entry type (Snapshot::use_snapshots() true) with a snapshot that records its input entries; three-node cluster after a decided StopSign, three reconnection rounds giving decided 9 over six indices of content, then snapshot(Some(8), false) on the leader. knowledge.statement: Both compaction paths derive the index they may compact from values the node computes for itself rather than from what any replica holds: trim takes the minimum of the accepted indexes the leader has recorded for the configuration (or refuses an explicit index above that minimum) and the snapshot path takes the decided index of the node that receives the call, while neither bound is compared against the entries the node's own log contains. knowledge.conditions: Capture snapshot; leader role for trim, any role for the snapshot call. knowledge.statement: The snapshot path adjustment for a request equal to the decided index is not a protection against the witnessed drift: that case maps the request to the decided log without the StopSign, which in the observed state was 8 against content of six indices, so the resulting compacted index still exceeded the entries the replica held and the snapshot was still built from an empty range.
knowledge.conditions: Snapshot-capable entry type after the drift; derived from try_snapshot and read against the sampled state of receipt e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c, where the decided index was 9 and the content six indices. No execution used a request exactly equal to the decided index.

semantic_changes: Driving the protocol without tick() means BLE heartbeats and resend timers never fire; that is deliberate so the reconnection path is the only recovery trigger.
Events are emitted as single-line CA_EVENT JSON objects on stdout; SAMPLE carries the case and phase so both cases in one execution stay separable.

scope.description: Two cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network: (resync) re-established connections to the leader after a decided StopSign, (control) identical prefix without reconnected(). Only public API calls drive the protocol; every observation is one CA_EVENT JSON line on stdout.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot, so T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() is false and create_log_sync takes its no-snapshot branch.
ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } (majority 2) and default ServerConfig (batch_size 1, no batching).
Leadership is established with the public try_become_leader() on node 3; BLE heartbeat messages are dropped because no tick() is called.
All SequencePaxos messages are delivered in FIFO order without loss, so the reconnection and re-synchronization is the only deviation from a healthy run.
Case labels in the events ('case') keep the resync and control streams distinguishable.
excluded: Snapshots, trimming and compaction are not exercised; batching is disabled (batch_size 1).
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

basis.prefix: Cluster::new() builds OmniPaxos<Value, MemoryStorage<Value>> for pids 1,2,3 (validated OmniPaxosConfig). run_prefix(): node 3 calls try_become_leader(); the FIFO pump drains Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync/Accepted until quiet (SAMPLE phase leader_elected); node 3 appends Value(0..4) and the pump drains AcceptDecide/Accepted/Decide until quiet (phase entries_decided); node 3 calls reconfigure(ClusterConfig{configuration_id: 2, nodes:[1,2,3]}, None) and the pump drains AcceptStopSign/Accepted/Decide until quiet (phase stopsign_decided). Case resync then calls node1.reconnected(3) and node2.reconnected(3) and pumps to quiet; case control only pumps again. Each SAMPLE line reports node, accepted_idx (get_accepted_idx), decided_idx (get_decided_idx), decided_eq_accepted, is_reconfigured(), read(5), and read_decided_suffix(0) (state plus entry count).
basis.responsibility: Target-internal bookkeeping: SequencePaxos::create_log_sync plus InternalStorage::sync_log decide what a re-synchronized replica's accepted index and carried StopSign are; the caller only reports a re-established connection through the public reconnected() API and never supplies log indices or StopSign state.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading of the re-synchronization path (PrepareReq -> Prepare -> Promise -> AcceptSync -> Accepted) suggests that a replica which has accepted the StopSign gets its accepted index inflated by one when it is re-synchronized at the same ballot: in handle_promise_accept the leader calls send_accsync, whose first branch uses the follower's own accepted index as the valid prefix (leader.rs 150-191), and that index already includes the StopSign because set_stopsign adds it (internal_storage.rs 503-512). create_log_sync then reports that index as LogSync.sync_idx with the sender's StopSign attached, and sync_log adds the StopSign once more, so the follower's accepted index ends at prefix + suffix + 1 while its decided index is the AcceptSync's decided index (internal_storage.rs 313-360). The follower then reports that inflated index in Accepted (follower.rs 112-126), and the leader's decision rule accepts any incoming accepted index whose count reaches a write quorum (leader.rs 316-345), so a write quorum of inflated reports would set the leader's decided index past the entries it holds. Both endpoints this reading endangers are public: is_reconfigured() is gated on stopsign_is_decided() (mod.rs 284-290, state_cache.rs 123-126), the bool of LogEntry::StopSign is documented as 'the reconfiguration has been decided' (util.rs 277-279), and the documented user flow reads the decided suffix and switches configuration only on StopSign(.., true) (reconfiguration.md 25-34). The final judgment is left unresolved until the two-case execution samples the endpoints; the reading also predicts that a fresh or lagging follower, whose prefix does not yet contain the StopSign, is unaffected. Counterevidence and limits: the reconfiguration documentation tells the user to start a new instance once the StopSign is observed as decided, so the affected window is an old instance that keeps running after (or while) it observes the decision and then re-synchronizes; the accounting is correct whenever sync_idx stays at or below the StopSign's own index, which covers the normal catch-up path; the account rests on static reading of the read() combination paths and of MemoryStorage's empty-range behaviour, not on an executed observation.

Confirmed by execution: the re-synchronization of a replica that already accepted its configuration's StopSign inflates its reported accepted index by one, and a write quorum of such reports makes the leader decide an index past every entry it holds. Receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8, two cases in one run over three real OmniPaxos instances with MemoryStorage (events: 19,20,21 = after the StopSign was decided on all three nodes; 22,23 = the two re-synchronized followers; 24 = the leader; 9,10,11 = the identical prefix without reconnected()). Before the re-synchronization all three nodes reported accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, read(5) = StopSign with decided = true, and read_decided_suffix(0) = six elements. After both followers called reconnected(3): node 1 and node 2 reported accepted 7 over the same six indices of content, their read(5) returned None (the StopSign is now placed at index 6 by the internal index-type rule), and their decided-log read from 0 returned a single element (the StopSign), so the five decided entries disappeared from the readable decided log while is_reconfigured stayed true; node 3 (leader) reported decided 7 with accepted 6, is_reconfigured false where it had been true, read(5) = StopSign with decided = false, and read_decided_suffix(0) = None, i.e. the user on the leader can no longer read the decided log at all and never observes the reconfiguration as complete. The declared comparisons match this reading: comparison 2 (leader reports the reconfiguration as decided) violated at index 24, comparison 3 (decided index covered by entries held) violated at index 24, comparison 4 (leader's decided log readable from 0) violated at index 24, comparison 5 (re-synchronized follower's decided log still has the five entries plus the StopSign) violated at indices 22 and 23, while comparisons 0 and 1 (the same predicates before the reconnection, indices 19-21) and comparisons 6 and 7 (the no-reconnect control, indices 9-11) hold, which attributes the change to the re-synchronization rather than to the reconfiguration or to the sampling.

27bf7fc0875c4342966bd3dc15df80ec-gap-0.explanation: The legitimate producer path was observed end to end: node 1 and node 2 each called the public reconnected(3) after the StopSign had been accepted and decided; reconnected() sets the follower to Phase::Recover and sends PrepareReq with its current promise (agent-source/omnipaxos/src/sequence_paxos/mod.rs 343-357); the leader in Phase::Accept handles it via handle_preparereq, resets the follower's promise state and re-sends Prepare (leader.rs 66-74); the follower, now in Phase::Recover with its promise equal to the Prepare's ballot, re-promises with accepted_idx = 6, an index that already counts its stored StopSign (follower.rs 13-51, internal_storage.rs 503-512); handle_promise_accept then calls send_accsync (leader.rs 301-314), and because the promise's accepted round equals the leader's current ballot, send_accsync takes its first branch and uses the follower's own accepted index as the valid prefix (leader.rs 150-191), producing LogSync{sync_idx: 6, suffix: [], stopsign: Some} from create_log_sync (mod.rs 405-432); sync_log then adds the StopSign once more (internal_storage.rs 313-360). Receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 confirms the outcome on the sampled endpoints (events 22 and 23).

knowledge.assertion: sync_log double-counts the StopSign when the resumed prefix already contains it
a re-synchronized replica's decided log read shrinks to the StopSign alone

counterevidence: The no-reconnect control case of the same execution kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read at indices 9-11), so the deviation is attributable to the re-established-connection path and not to the reconfiguration, to the harness, or to reading the log.

The documented user flow for reconfiguration (agent-source/docs/omnipaxos/reconfiguration.md 25-34) expects the user to start a new instance once a node observes LogEntry::StopSign(ss, true); a user who stops the old instance immediately limits the user-facing window, but does not remove the defect: the leader of the same run never observes the StopSign as decided after the corruption (is_reconfigured false, decided log unreadable), and the two followers keep reporting the reconfiguration as decided while their decided log silently loses the five decided entries.

The leader's phantom decision is inferred from its own reported state (decided 7 with accepted 6 and six indices of content) plus the two followers' inflated 7; the internal accepted-index vector was not sampled, so the assignment of which reports formed the quorum rests on the source rule (handle_accepted decides any incoming accepted index reaching a write quorum) rather than on a direct trace of that vector.
limitations: No snapshots (NoSnapshot entries) and default batch size 1: whether the snapshot-enabled branch of create_log_sync inflates the same way is untested.

interpretations.rationale: Source trace only, no execution. handle_majority_promises pairs two independently ordered inputs: the log_sync of the promise that is strictly greatest under (n_accepted, accepted_idx) (set_promise only replaces max_promise_meta on a strict Greater, and PromiseMetaData's ordering ignores decided_idx) and the maximum decided_idx across all recorded promises (get_max_decided_idx). sync_log then stores the adopted decided index together with the adopted log and does not clamp. The candidate's accepted index after the prepare phase is determined by the adopted promise: with the resume point inside that promise's content the candidate ends at exactly the adopted promise's accepted count, because the suffix supplies the entries from the resume point to that content and the carried StopSign adds the same one index the adopted promise had already counted (the follower's Promise sets common_prefix to the candidate's decided index when its accepted round is higher, and to the candidate's accepted index when the rounds are equal and it is further ahead); with the resume point beyond that content the suffix is empty and the candidate ends at the resume point plus the StopSign term. (2) The index drifts one step per re-synchronization round rather than settling: three consecutive reconnection rounds took the followers from 7 to 8 to 9 over unchanged content and the leader's decided index followed (6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d events 41-49).
